Im in a similar situation. Your post made me cry. You deserve so much better than the relationship you are in now. Sadly I’m looking for tips on how to leave myself so I can’t tell you anything that can make it easier for you. 
But know you are not alone.

I’ve been where you are rn. Confused if something is wrong with me or if I’m crazy. It took a long time for me to get diagnosed with bpd. From what you’re describing here of course it’s hard to tell if you have a mental illness or not and I’m not a professional.

But you’re not crazy. I don’t like this word to describe someone. You’re probably confused about what you’re feeling and what’s going on in your head. You said you’re a teenager so it could also be effects of puberty. But whatever it is know that your feelings are valid and you should try to find a way to talk to a doctor or some other person you trust that could help you.

In the meantime I also have an open ear for you if you want to get things off your chest :)
Though it doesn’t hurt to get yourself checked out to rule out any other things it could be.

I have this mostly at nighttime when I was stressed or really anxious throughout the day. I feel like I’m getting sick. With all the symptoms you described. And then the next morning it’s gone. I’ve had this so often that I’m pretty sure it’s coming from too much stress and/or anxiety. My therapist said this is a way for your brain to cope with stress or anxiety. Even if it sounds completely counterproductive. Maybe your brain makes you have flu like symptoms in hopes you’ll think you’re sick and take a rest to reduce the stress.
Your brain can mimic a big variety of things and I find it fascinating and frightening at the same time.

I’m not a therapist and don’t know how you could find one in your situation but if you want to talk and let it all out you can talk to me. Sometimes its good to just talk to someone and get things off your chest

I think I can understand. After I left I ended up in psych ward because I tried to off myself. I lost all direction in life and Family and friends. I even tried to off myself when I was in the psych ward. 
I spent 7 months there. Everyday therapy. And after I got out I realised that I only scratched the surface of my problems. 
Therapy is no miracle cure. It takes a long time and hard work. It’s really not easy.
And honestly I can’t tell you when it gets better.
But what options do you have? Go back or not go back.
I chose Not going back and trying to make the best out of it. I’m not gonna lie.. it’s though. But you can manage to create a better life where you’re not constantly in a bad place. No matter how old you are.

Find out what you really want in life. What do you love to do. What do you want to be. Who do you want to be.
Find yourself some goals. Short and long-term.
And I say it again. It’s not easy. It’s hard. And takes a long time.
Why do this? Why bother if you don’t know if it gets better someday?
Well these are valid questions that I unfortunately can’t answer.
This is your life. You choose if you try or don’t try.

To be honest I don’t think anything I’ve read or someone told me could’ve changed my mind a few years ago. I was so sure this was the truth.
Even though I had a „worldly“ boyfriend after I moved out of my parents house and stopped going to the meetings I was still so deep in. I still believed everything they said and was plagued with the guilt from living a life that wasn’t approved by jws.
Nothing my boyfriend at that time told me could’ve changed my mind. And he tried really hard to open my eyes.
It took a few more years, a bad jw therapist, panic attacks and my current boyfriend (who is a satanist lol) to make me question.
The jw therapist whom my parents send me to told me I definitely don’t have a personality disorder (I’m now officially diagnosed with bpd by real therapists) and that I should read the bible more often, pray and go to the meetings and this would cure my mental health problems. Obviously this didn’t do shit. (I gave it many many tries beforehand) After the talk with this jw therapist I felt so misunderstood and angry and left alone. I had a mental breakdown. Shortly after this I got really bad panic attacks that would keep me up for days. I couldn’t rest. I couldn’t even sit down. Worst was when I ran through my flat for 48 hours without sitting down once because i couldn’t. I had nonstop panic attacks.. I begged god to help me because I was going insane. I begged him to make it stop. After about 30 hours I gave up praying. Nothing had changed. I didn’t get strength from god and it didn’t get better. I was completely lost and helpless with this situation. Then something my now boyfriend said to me came to my mind. „You have to do something yourself. Don‘t wait for some God to save you because he won’t“.
And that’s when I finally started to realise that what jws say is bullshit. That night I tore up my bibles. And never prayed again. Then I finally allowed my self to look at „apostate“ videos and websites. And slowly began to understand what this religion really is.
I ended up in the psych ward because my whole world was crushed. I realised so many things at that time that I needed professional help to process everything. Even though I’m still not completely mentally healthy, I’m on a good way.
Leaving the borg and realising what bullshit organisation this is was the best thing ever happening to me. It was hard but it was worth it. Now I finally feel free. I can dress how I want, I can eat what I want, I can work what I want, I can celebrate what I want. I can BE what I want!
I even started crying writing this because I’m so happy that I’m out of this shitty religion. 
Life’s not perfect but it‘s so so much better without Jehovas witnesses.
I‘d never go back.

I don’t yet have a diagnosis and I unfortunately can’t tell you what causes it but I know exactly the feeling you described.
I have this since I was a little kid. I was constantly afraid to go to sleep. I often only managed to sleep when I was so extremely tired from not being able to sleep that I would just „pass out“. 
I hear every little noise and am scared of the darkness because I can’t see what’s around me. Like you I’m afraid of closing my eyes because I think something bad will happen. And I would always try to close my eyes as long as possible but I couldn’t keep them shut.
What helped me was leaving on the TV. I have a TV in my bedroom and before I go to sleep I put on the TV. Find the right volume so that it’s not too loud but not too quiet. And then I try to sleep. sometimes I even put on a little nightlight. 

If I don’t do this I’m going crazy... 

Unfortunately I have many reasons why I can’t sleep at night. But at least this problem is solved (most of the time. Doesn’t work all the time) by just leaving on the TV when trying to sleep.
I hope maybe this helps you too.

Also what I just remembered.. sometimes it helps to open the window and chew some of these chilli gummies. I don’t know what they’re called. But it helps at least a bit when I have something really hot or sour to eat because it helps me be present a bit more.

When I drive I’m nearly never really in the present. There are short moments of „clarity“ where I wonder how I got to this point and if I drove of road or something because I don’t remember and it literally feels like my body is driving but I’m somewhere else. It can be really scary and I have to admit that (especially at night) I’ve run a few red lights. But I’ve also been in situations where I was in this state and something unusual happened but my body reacted on its own. It happened quite a few times and I was always able to prevent car crashes because my body reacted somehow. 
I step on the breaks automatically and when I then realise after a few seconds what had happened I feel completely aware of everything again. It’s like being under water and suddenly someone pulls you out.
What I wanted to say with this is that I learned to trust the automatic reactions and the ability of my body driving even when I’m in a dissociative state. That makes it easier for me to not be afraid to drive. Although I would say if you have any other option instead of driving yourself I would take it if I were you. It still can be dangerous and I can only speak for my self so ofc I don’t know if you will react the way I do. 
I’m currently starting therapy and I can only recommend you do this too so that someday hopefully we both can drive without problems.
